correctness.rationale: At an interior exact phase a/b in lowest terms the response is 1 iff b divides k; irrational phases give no positives. For q=p^a, compare q to q/p: any probe that distinguishes them must divide q but not q/p in denominator, so that denominator must be q. Distinct q force distinct probes, and the 1/q construction reads all prime valuations, determining k. Comparing 1 to each prime forces prime denominators for the all-negative certificate, and they suffice. Grid denominators divide H, so all mandatory q are possible iff lcm(1,…,N) divides H. With a common tolerance, widened midpoint sets for q/p remain contained in those for q. A distinguishing probe must be within ε of an additional midpoint of reduced denominator q. Distinct midpoint phases mod 1 with denominators b,d≤N have circular distance at least 1/(bd): the shortest nonzero difference modulo 1 is a nonzero integral multiple of 1/(bd). Thus 2ε<1/N² still makes different q witnesses disjoint, and probing precisely at 1/q still rejects all aliases not divisible by q. The common phase 0 is not a distinguishing midpoint. This proves the statements also at N=2 and ε=0; the grid iff is not asserted for ε>0. The independent exact-Fraction replay `/workspace/branches/604c4515-7044-487c-828f-b07004adbef6/record4_independent_replay.py` checked signatures, forced denominators, certificates and circular-tolerance signatures at N=12 and 38. It obtained (Q_N,π(N),L_N)=(8,5,27720) and (19,12,5342931457063200); these are finite checks, with the quantifiers settled by the proof.

value.rationale: For an existing astronomical alias problem the result distinguishes the number of actual measurements from regular-grid resolution, which can be much larger even in a modest candidate range. It gives a universal lower bound and construction, distinguishes certification from full identification, and shows the count is not merely an artifact of demanding exact midpoint detections. The separation is scientifically interpretable within the stated idealization; it is not a recommended instrument cadence or a claim about noisy, pruned or adaptive campaigns.
